input.objective:
Launch Pondside (POND) with a Uniswap v4 hook on Sepolia, paired with ETH.
Token: Pondside (POND), the standard launch token: 1,000,000,000 supply, 18 decimals, plain transfers, no owner functions.
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. Take 1.0% of the ETH side of every buy and sell as a hook fee, settled in ETH inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly), and send it to my wallet. Expose claimFees() that anyone may call to redeem claims to the recipient.
2. The hook fee starts at 10.0% of the ETH side of every swap when the pool opens and decreases linearly to 1.0% over the first 30 minutes, then stays at 1.0%. Expose currentFeeBps() as a view.
3. Any swap whose ETH side is larger than 1 ETH pays an extra 1.0% of its ETH side as a hook fee, on top of any other hook fee, settled the same way and sent to the same recipient.
4. When the pool price has moved more than 5.0% within the last 20 blocks, the hook fee on the ETH side of every swap is 3.0% until the move settles below that; otherwise the normal hook fee applies. Expose isVolatile() as a view.
5. Split every hook fee: 70% to my wallet and 30% to 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000.
6. For the first 10 minutes after the pool opens, each wallet may buy at most 1.0% of the total supply in total; larger buys revert. Expose windowEndsAt() as a view.
7. Each wallet may buy at most 2.0% of the total supply through this pool in total, for the life of the pool; larger buys revert. Sells are never blocked. Expose boughtBy(address) as a view.
8. Reject any single swap whose specified amount is above 1,000,000 POND, in either direction. This caps only the amount the swapper specifies.
9. Protect swappers from sandwich attacks: within one block, swaps against the direction of the block’s first swap execute at no better than the block’s opening price (the AntiSandwichHook pattern).
10. A wallet must wait at least 30 seconds between its swaps in this pool. Expose nextSwapAt(address) as a view.
11. If the pool price moves more than 20% within 10 blocks, reject every swap for the next 5 minutes, then resume automatically. Liquidity can still be removed during the pause. Expose haltedUntil() as a view.
12. Collect 1.0% of the ETH side of every swap into a jar held by the hook. Whenever the jar holds at least 0.1 ETH, anyone may call buyback() to buy POND from this pool with the whole jar and burn the bought tokens. The swap that fills the jar does not revert if the buyback fails. Expose jar() as a view.
13. Collect 2.0% of the ETH side of every buy into a prize pot. Every 1 hour(s), anyone may call draw() to pay the whole pot to one buyer from that period chosen at random, weighted by how much ETH each buyer spent; randomness comes from recent block data, which is acceptable for small pots and must be stated in the README. Expose pot() and nextDrawAt() as views.
No owner functions, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the ETH (pair currency) side, never from POND; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem.
Enable beforeInitialize (required by the IMD launch factory) and only the callbacks the behavior above needs. Take the PoolManager as a constructor argument. Owner, if any, is $owner.
Pool: 50% of my 90% share seeds the pool; the remainder goes to the paying wallet.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.
